record.title: Authors report higher ARC-AGI-3 solve rates from test-time agent communication in a bounded setup
record.summary: A September 17 preprint compares shared-workspace teams with independent parallel agents on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games. Using Claude Sonnet 4.6, the authors report full-game solve rates of 4.6% for teams of three and 8.0% for teams of five, versus 1.4% and 2.2% for the best of three and five independent attempts. Matching the reported team solve rates required 13 and 33 independent attempts, respectively. The paper also reports gains on two research-oriented tasks, but says communication can lose under limited compute or unclear feedback. These are author-reported results from one model and benchmark setup; the research desk did not reproduce them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games using Claude Sonnet 4.6, the authors report full-game solve rates of 4.6% for team@3 and 8.0% for team@5, versus 1.4% for best@3 and 2.2% for best@5; matching those team rates required 13 and 33 independent attempts, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports transfer gains on polyomino packing and MNIST classifier compression, and reports no advantage over independent pass@2 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 when intermediate feedback does not reliably rank progress.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish that the reported advantage generalizes to other models, tasks, larger teams, deployment workloads, or settings without objective progress feedback; the research desk did not reproduce the results.

evidence_gaps.description: The ARC-AGI-3 team and independent success rates are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
The principal comparison covers one model, public ARC games and team sizes three and five; generalization to other models, task regimes and larger teams is unknown.
The paper reports different polyomino packing scores in its introduction and Table 1 (0.922 versus 0.945).

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded result is replicated, communication may produce substantially more solved open-ended tasks per parallel attempt and alter inference-budget design. The 5/10 score reflects relevance across agent research, while the narrow task/model regime and lack of independent reproduction limit the justified consequence.
limitations: Results are author-reported from a single preprint; the research desk did not reproduce them.
The primary ARC result is limited to Claude Sonnet 4.6, 25 public games and team sizes of three and five.
The paper describes a coordination tax when compute is limited or progress is hard to verify; Terminal-Bench 2.0 team@2 did not outperform independent pass@2.
A polyomino packing score differs between the introduction and Table 1 (0.922 versus 0.945); that transfer result is not treated as resolved.
brief.summary: A September 17 preprint compares shared-workspace teams with independent parallel agents on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games. Using Claude Sonnet 4.6, the authors report full-game solve rates of 4.6% for teams of three and 8.0% for teams of five, versus 1.4% and 2.2% for the best of three and five independent attempts. Matching the reported team solve rates required 13 and 33 independent attempts, respectively. The paper also reports gains on two research-oriented tasks, but says communication can lose under limited compute or unclear feedback. These are author-reported results from one model and benchmark setup; the research desk did not reproduce them.

technical.claimed_result: On ARC-AGI-3, team@3 reports 4.6% full-game solves and team@5 8.0%, compared with best@3 1.4% and best@5 2.2%; matching team solve rates took best@13 and best@33. The result is author-reported.
technical.compute_or_cost: The ARC comparison uses team sizes 3 and 5 against independent pools of 13 and 33 to match reported solve rates. Absolute token, monetary and energy costs are not reported in the inspected result summary, and equal per-agent resources do not establish equal total cost for the larger independent pools.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 paper documents the protocol, sample design, reported outcomes and limitations. It does not independently demonstrate those outcomes; the research desk did not execute the harness or reproduce any benchmark.
technical.mechanism: Identical agents work on the same open-ended objective with separate contexts and a shared workspace where they post intermediate results, failures and artifacts. Team members may adopt a peer approach after observing a measured improvement; objective benchmark feedback is used to decide what to retain.
technical.regime: ARC-AGI-3 public suite: 25 games, Claude Sonnet 4.6, 64 single-agent trials per game and 20 trials for each team size/game combination; team sizes k=3 and k=5; native per-level action budgets. Additional experiments cover polyomino packing and MNIST compression under different models and compute budgets.
technical.strongest_baseline: Best-of-k independent attempts using Claude Sonnet 4.6 on the same 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games: 1.4% at k=3 and 2.2% at k=5, versus team rates of 4.6% and 8.0%. The paper also compares team@k with larger independent pools of 13 and 33 attempts.

brief.title: Authors report higher ARC-AGI-3 solve rates from test-time agent communication in a bounded setup
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported advantage survives independent evaluation, sharing verified partial discoveries could change how inference budgets are allocated for open-ended agent tasks. The evidence covers one model on 25 public games and team sizes of three and five, and the paper itself identifies a coordination tax when compute or progress feedback is inadequate.
